TFDL_AD: The campus writing center has updated its drop-in tutoring policy for the fall term. Beginning September 5, students may sign up for a thirty-minute session either online through the center's booking portal or in person at the front desk on the day of their visit. Each appointment is limited to one student and one tutor, and the center asks that students bring a draft of at least one page so that tutors can give focused feedback. Tutors will not review work longer than eight pages during a single visit, and they cannot read assignments that have not yet been started. Sessions are offered Monday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Friday from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The center is closed on weekends and on university holidays.

Students who arrive more than ten minutes late will be counted as no-shows, and a second no-show in the same term will block further bookings for the rest of that term. The center reminds visitors that tutors can help with thesis development, organization, grammar, and citation, but they do not proofread entire papers, and they cannot guarantee improved grades. Walk-in students without an appointment will be seated only if a tutor happens to be free, so the center strongly recommends reserving a slot in advance.

Because demand is high in October, the center is also piloting small-group workshops on academic paragraph structure. Each workshop lasts forty-five minutes, welcomes up to six students, and requires preregistration through the same booking portal. Workshop topics rotate weekly and are listed on the center's website, and students who miss two workshops without canceling will lose workshop privileges for the remainder of the term, although they can still use regular tutoring sessions.
